name_story.story: Ayub can be understood through the Arabic form أَيُّوب, whose central sense is ayub; job (prophet). Ayub is Arabic أَيُّوب (Ayyūb), the Quranic form of the prophet Job.

faq.a: Ayub is associated with the Arabic form أَيُّوب, whose core sense is ayub; job (prophet).

faq.q: What is the origin of Ayub?
faq.a: Ayub is associated with Arabic. Ayub is Arabic أَيُّوب (Ayyūb), the Quranic form of the prophet Job.
Yes — the underlying form أَيُّوب is Arabic.
Ayub can occur in Muslim naming contexts, but it is better described as a Arabic-origin name used within some Muslim naming traditions than as an exclusively Islamic religious term.
Ayub should not be classified as a Quranic personal name without a direct Quranic basis. Ayyūb is the Quranic Arabic form of the prophet Job and occurs in the Quran.

faq.a: In Urdu, Ayub is rendered ایوب and carries the sense ایوب، نبی کا نام.

faq.q: What does Ayub mean in Persian?
faq.a: In Persian, Ayub is rendered ایوب and carries the sense ایوب، نام پیامبر.
A romanized syllable approximation is ayub. No IPA transcription is asserted because a verified phonetic transcription was not available.

faq.q: What are the variants of Ayub?
faq.a: Romanization variants include Ayub, ayub. Script forms are أَيُّوب, ايوب, ایوب, अय्यूब.

faq.q: Is Ayub a boy's or girl's name?
faq.a: Documented usage records this form as male. Gender is not inferred from the meaning of the word, and actual use may vary between communities.
